newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Platinum miners locked out at Lonrho mine.
newsitem.headline: Platinum miners locked out at Lonrho mine.

text.p: About 9,000 workers at Lonrho's Western Platinum mine have been locked out since Friday after staging a two-hour protest action, South Africa's National Union of Mineworkers said on Tuesday.

"The dispute is over the way the acting underground manager conducted himself...He changed the underground regulations without consulting the (workers') shaft committee," union spokesman Ben Molapo told Reuters.
He said the union was in negotiations with management to find a solution.
A Lonrho spokesman said workers took the acting manager hostage on Thursday night and assaulted him.
"We decided to lock out workers until we get assurances for people's safety," Lonrho spokesman Tony Frost told Reuters.
He said the mine produced 160,000 tonnes of ore per month and four days of production had been lost due to the action.
Lonrho platinum division's three mines in South Africa produced around 570,000 ounces of platinum in 1995.
